result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would remove the evolutionary hardwiring that makes humans instinctively fear and distrust the unfamiliar. 

Much of the world’s suffering—from tribalism and war to systemic injustice and everyday cruelty—stems from a primitive, default reaction to things that are different: different beliefs, different appearances, different ways of living. 

If human nature were fundamentally wired to approach the unknown with baseline curiosity and empathy rather than suspicion and defense, cooperation would become our path of least resistance. Empathy wouldn’t require effort; it would just be the way the world works.
